title: Approach to Stall or Stall Recovery

flash.title: Base turn, flaps 5, A/P engaged, night.
flash.text: ATC kept you high, speedbrakes still out. In the turn the speed bleeds below the amber band and the column starts to shake.

steps.text: Hold the control column firmly.
Disengage autopilot and autothrottle.
Smoothly apply nose down elevator to reduce the angle of attack until buffet or stick shaker stops. Nose down stabilizer trim can be needed.
Roll in the shortest direction to wings level if needed.
Advance thrust levers as needed.
Retract the speedbrakes.
Do not change gear or flap configuration, except — During liftoff, if flaps are up, call for flaps 1.
Set the FLAP lever as directed.
Check airspeed and adjust thrust as needed. Establish pitch attitude. Return to the desired flight path.
Re-engage the autopilot and autothrottle if desired.
Monitor altitude and airspeed. Verify all needed actions have been done and call out any omissions. Call out any trend toward terrain contact.

trap: Trying to “save altitude” by holding back pressure. Reduce AOA first (column forward, nose-down trim if needed, not excessive) — and no FD during the recovery.
then: Back to commanded speed, thrust adjusted, flight path regained
Re-engage A/P and A/T per normal procedures
Smooth pull-out: too aggressive a pull up → secondary stall
Thrust already high (T/O, G/A): a reduction may be needed to lower AOA
PM: calls out any trend toward terrain
diff: Same maneuver NG/MAX (QRH MAN.1.1). Wording nuance: “Nose down stabilizer trim may be needed” (QRH NG) / “can be needed” (QRH MAX).

qcm.q: Stick shaker in the base turn, A/P engaged. PF's first action per QRH?
qcm.w: Initiate the recovery starts with “Hold the control column firmly”, then disengage A/P and A/T, then nose down elevator.

qcm.q: During the recovery, flight directors are:
qcm.w: QRH: “Do not use flight director commands during the recovery.” FDs are not designed to guide a stall recovery (FCTM 7.14).

qcm.q: Shaker at liftoff, flaps retracted by mistake. Configuration?
qcm.w: Only exception to “Do not change gear or flap configuration”: “During liftoff, if flaps are up, call for flaps 1.”

qcm.q: Elevator alone won't lower the nose. Nose-down trim:
o: Must be run to full nose down
Is done with the trim wheel only
qcm.w: “Nose down stabilizer trim can be needed” — but excessive trim can worsen the situation or lead to loss of control (QRH WARNING).

qcm.q: Approach to stall near FL350. What does the FCTM say?
o: Max thrust is enough, no altitude loss
qcm.w: Above about 20,000 ft the airplane is thrust limited: nose down + trim to descend; the recovery costs more altitude.

sources.quote: Immediately do the following at the first indication of stall (buffet or stick shaker). Note: Do not use flight director commands during the recovery.
Do not change gear or flap configuration, except • During liftoff, if flaps are up, call for flaps 1.
Smoothly apply nose down elevator to reduce the angle of attack until buffet or stick shaker stops. Nose down stabilizer trim may be needed.
At higher altitudes, normally above 20,000 feet, the airplane becomes increasingly thrust limited.
If an erroneous stick shaker is activated continuously and airspeed is V2 or greater and vertical speed is positive, continue climbout to acceleration height

title: Ground Proximity Warning System (GPWS) Response — GPWS Warning

flash.title: Night arrival, high terrain around the field, IMC.
flash.text: Descent clearance misunderstood, you go below sector altitude. The radio altimeter is unwinding and the cockpit is screaming.
cues: Red PULL UP on both PFDs

steps.text: Call “TERRAIN GO” (Air Algérie SOP)
Disengage autopilot.
Disengage autothrottle.
Aggressively apply maximum thrust.
Simultaneously roll wings level and rotate to an initial pitch attitude of 20°.
Retract speedbrakes.
If terrain remains a threat, continue rotation up to the pitch limit indicator (if available) or stick shaker or initial buffet.
Do not change gear or flap configuration until terrain separation is assured.
Monitor radio altimeter for sustained or increasing terrain separation.
When clear of terrain, slowly decrease pitch attitude and accelerate.
Assure maximum thrust. Verify all needed actions have been completed and call out any omissions.
Monitor vertical speed and altitude (radio altitude for terrain clearance and barometric altitude for a minimum safe altitude.) Call out any trend toward terrain contact.

nums.s: Then up to PLI / shaker if threat remains

trap: Keeping the A/P or following the FD: the QRH says “Do not use flight director commands”. And don't touch gear/flaps until terrain separation is assured.
then: Threat gone: call terrain no longer a factor (SOP)
Slowly decrease pitch, accelerate, retract gear/flaps per schedule
Do not re-engage A/P or A/T until terrain separation is assured (FCTM)
Look-ahead alert in climb/cruise/descent, verified above MSA: may be considered unreliable
GPWS Caution (SINK RATE, TERRAIN, GLIDESLOPE…): “Correct the flight path, airplane configuration, or airspeed.”
diff: Same maneuver NG/MAX. On NG, the “OBSTACLE OBSTACLE PULL UP” / CAUTION OBSTACLE alert exists only on airplanes YD108–YD117, YG721–YV388 (QRH NG effectivity).

qcm.q: “TERRAIN TERRAIN PULL UP” at night in IMC. Target initial pitch?
qcm.w: GPWS warning: “rotate to an initial pitch attitude of 20°”. 15° is the windshear escape.

qcm.q: Terrain still a threat after 20°. How far to pitch up?
o: Up to PLI, or stick shaker, or initial buffet
qcm.w: “continue rotation up to the pitch limit indicator (if available) or stick shaker or initial buffet.” Intermittent shaker is the upper limit.

qcm.q: During the maneuver, gear and flaps:
o: No change until terrain separation is assured
qcm.w: “Do not change gear or flap configuration until terrain separation is assured.”

qcm.q: PM's role on thrust?
qcm.w: PM: “Assure maximum thrust”, verifies actions and calls out omissions. The PF has already disengaged the A/T.

qcm.q: PF's Air Algérie SOP callout when initiating the maneuver?
qcm.w: SOP 3.3: “When the GPWS Warning Maneuver is required, the PF shall call: "TERRAIN GO"”.

sources.quote: Aggressively apply maximum* thrust. Simultaneously roll wings level and rotate to an initial pitch attitude of 20°.
If terrain remains a threat, continue rotation up to the pitch limit indicator (if available) or stick shaker or initial buffet.
Note: Do not use flight director commands.
Do not attempt to engage the autopilot or autothrottle until terrain clearance is assured.
When the GPWS Warning Maneuver is required, the PF shall call: "TERRAIN GO"
TERRAIN, TERRAIN, PULL UP … 20 to 30 seconds from projected impact

title: Traffic Avoidance

flash.title: Climbing to FL240, A/P engaged, busy TMA.
flash.text: TA first, then the traffic converges. TCAS commands a maneuver just as ATC gives you a different instruction.
cues: Red zone on the vertical speed/attitude indicator

steps.text: Look for traffic using traffic display as a guide. If traffic is sighted, maneuver if needed.
Call out any conflicting traffic.

steps.phase: For RA (except a climb in landing configuration)
steps.text: If maneuvering is needed, disengage the autopilot and autothrottle.
Smoothly adjust pitch and thrust to satisfy the RA command. Follow the planned lateral flight path unless visual contact with the conflicting traffic requires other action.
Attempt to establish visual contact.
Call out any conflicting traffic.
For a climb RA in landing configuration: Disengage the autopilot and autothrottle. Advance thrust levers forward to ensure maximum thrust is attained and call for FLAPS 15.
Verify maximum thrust set. Position flap lever to 15 detent.
Smoothly adjust pitch to satisfy the RA command. Follow the planned lateral flight path unless visual contact with the conflicting traffic requires other action.
Verify a positive rate of climb on the altimeter and call “GEAR UP.”
Verify a positive rate of climb on the altimeter and call “POSITIVE RATE.” Set the landing gear lever to UP.

nums.s: Do not follow a DESCEND RA below

trap: Following ATC instead of the RA, or maneuvering opposite: “Comply with the RA if there is a conflict between the RA and air traffic control.” And no maneuver on a TA alone.
then: No FD pitch commands until clear of conflict
Shaker or initial buffet during the RA → Approach to Stall Recovery immediately
High-speed buffet: relax pitch-up force but continue the maneuver
Clear of conflict: promptly and smoothly return to cleared altitude/speed
Air Algérie TCAS II v7.1: “LEVEL OFF, LEVEL OFF” = reduce V/S to 0
diff: Same maneuver NG/MAX. The whole Air Algérie fleet has TCAS II v7.1 (SOP): the old “ADJUST VERTICAL SPEED ADJUST” RA is replaced by “LEVEL OFF”.

qcm.q: “CLIMB” RA just after ATC cleared you to descend. Action?
qcm.w: QRH WARNING: “Comply with the RA if there is a conflict between the RA and air traffic control.”

qcm.q: Below what height do you NOT follow a DESCEND RA?
qcm.w: “Do not follow a DESCEND (fly down) RA issued below 1000 feet AGL.”

qcm.q: Climb RA on final, landing config. Flaps called by PF?
qcm.w: “Advance thrust levers forward to ensure maximum thrust is attained and call for FLAPS 15.” Then GEAR UP on positive rate.

qcm.q: “TRAFFIC, TRAFFIC” TA, traffic not in sight. Action?
o: Look for traffic using the display, no maneuver on the TA alone
qcm.w: For a TA: look for the traffic. “Maneuvers based solely on a TA can result in reduced separation and are not recommended.”

qcm.q: Stick shaker during a climb RA. Priority?
o: Continue the RA, it has priority
qcm.w: QRH Note: shaker or initial buffet → “immediately accomplish the APPROACH TO STALL RECOVERY procedure”. The shaker comes first (FCTM).

sources.quote: WARNING: Comply with the RA if there is a conflict between the RA and air traffic control.
WARNING: Do not follow a DESCEND (fly down) RA issued below 1000 feet AGL.
Advance thrust levers forward to ensure maximum thrust is attained and call for FLAPS 15.
Windshear, GPWS, and stall warnings take precedence over TCAS advisories. Stick shaker must take priority at all times.
AIR ALGERIE airplanes are equipped with TCAS II version 7.1, the “ADJUST VERTICAL SPEED ADJUST” RA is replaced by “LEVEL OFF”.
confining vertical speeds to less than 1000 ft/min, and ideally a maximum of 1000 ft/min, within the last 2000 ft before reaching assigned level.

title: Upset Recovery — Nose High Recovery

flash.title: Cruise FL370, clear air turbulence.
flash.text: A vertical gust and the A/P trips off. The nose goes 30° above the horizon, speed collapsing.
cues: Mostly blue sky on the ADI

steps.text: Recognize and confirm the developing situation
Disengage autopilot.
Disengage autothrottle.
Apply nose-down elevator. Apply as much elevator as needed to obtain a nose down pitch rate
Apply appropriate nose down stabilizer trim
Reduce thrust
Roll (adjust bank angle) to obtain a nose down pitch rate.
When approaching the horizon, roll to wings level
Check airspeed and adjust thrust
Establish pitch attitude.
Call out attitude, airspeed and altitude throughout the recovery. Verify all needed actions have been done and call out any continued deviation.

nums.s: If pitch alone won't lower the nose (FCTM)

trap: Adding full thrust because speed is dropping: with underwing engines, thrust pitches the nose up further. Reduce thrust and push; trim only as needed — excessive trim or rudder worsens the upset.
then: Stalled? Recover from the stall first (nose down until shaker stops)
Stop nose-down trim when g or column force decreases
Rudder: only if roll control is ineffective and not stalled, small amounts
Near the horizon: wings level, speed, thrust, pitch

qcm.q: Nose high 30°, speed dropping. Thrust action?
qcm.w: QRH: “Reduce thrust”. Underwing engines: more thrust = additional nose-up moment.

qcm.q: Nose-down elevator and trim aren't enough. Next QRH step?
o: Roll (adjust bank angle) to obtain a nose down pitch rate
qcm.w: “Roll (adjust bank angle) to obtain a nose down pitch rate.” The FCTM cites 45°, up to 60° max.

qcm.q: When do you roll wings level?
o: Immediately at the start of the recovery
qcm.w: Complete the recovery: “When approaching the horizon, roll to wings level”, then speed/thrust, pitch.

qcm.q: Historically, a nose-high upset is a pitch attitude greater than:
qcm.w: Pitch > 25° nose up, > 10° nose down, bank > 45°, or inappropriate airspeed. Today: any deviation from the desired state.

qcm.q: PM's role during the recovery?
o: Call out attitude, airspeed and altitude throughout the recovery
Re-engage the A/P as soon as possible
qcm.w: PM: calls out attitude, airspeed and altitude throughout, verifies actions and calls out any continued deviation.

sources.quote: Apply nose-down elevator. Apply as much elevator as needed to obtain a nose down pitch rate • Apply appropriate nose down stabilizer trim* • Reduce thrust • Roll (adjust bank angle) to obtain a nose down pitch rate.*
When approaching the horizon, roll to wings level • Check airspeed and adjust thrust • Establish pitch attitude.
Pitch attitude greater than 25 degrees nose up • Pitch attitude greater than 10 degrees nose down • Bank angle greater than 45 degrees
Bank angles of about 45°, up to a maximum of 60°, could be needed.
the pitch rate should be controlled by modifying control inputs to maintain between 0 g and 1 g.

title: Upset Recovery — Nose Low Recovery

flash.title: Descent FL200, IMC, night.
flash.text: Display failure on the PF side, disorientation. When you get your scan back, the airplane is at 100° bank, nose below the horizon, speed climbing toward VMO.

steps.text: Recognize and confirm the developing situation
Disengage autopilot.
Disengage autothrottle.
Recover from stall, if needed
Roll in the shortest direction to wings level. If bank angle is more than 90 degrees, unload and roll.
Apply nose up elevator
Apply nose up trim, if needed
Adjust thrust and drag, if needed.
Call out attitude, airspeed and altitude throughout the recovery. Verify all needed actions have been done and call out any continued deviation.

nums.s: Beyond: level flight impossible within g limits (FCTM)

trap: Pulling before rolling wings level: beyond 60° bank, pulling barely changes pitch and loads the structure. Roll first (shortest direction, toward the bank pointer), then pull out.
then: The bank pointer stays perpendicular to the horizon: roll toward it
No nose-up elevator or nose-up trim until approaching wings level (FCTM)
Speedbrakes as needed to control speed
Control forces higher than normal: firm, continuous force

qcm.q: Bank 110°, nose low. The QRH action?
o: Pull to bring the nose to the horizon
Reduce thrust and extend the gear
Unload and roll, shortest direction to wings level
qcm.w: “Roll in the shortest direction to wings level. If bank angle is more than 90 degrees, unload and roll.”

qcm.q: Correct sequence, nose low:
o: Nose up elevator, then roll wings level
Roll wings level, then nose up elevator
qcm.w: Recover: stall if needed, roll wings level. Complete the recovery: nose up elevator, trim if needed, thrust/drag.

qcm.q: Before any upset recovery action, if the airplane is stalled:
o: Recover from the stall first (nose down)
qcm.w: QRH: “If the airplane is stalled, first recover from the stall by applying and maintaining nose down elevator until stall recovery is complete and stick shaker stops.”

qcm.q: Beyond what bank angle is level flight impossible within AFM load factor limits?
qcm.w: FCTM 7.25: “At bank angles greater than 67°, level flight cannot be maintained within AFM load factor limits.”

qcm.q: Rudder use during an upset:
o: Always, to speed up the roll
Only if roll control is ineffective and not stalled, carefully
qcm.w: QRH: “Careful use of rudder to aid roll control should be considered only if roll control is ineffective and the airplane is not stalled.”

sources.quote: Roll in the shortest direction to wings level. If bank angle is more than 90 degrees, unload and roll.*
Apply nose up elevator • Apply nose up trim, if needed* • Adjust thrust and drag, if needed.
If the airplane is stalled, first recover from the stall by applying and maintaining nose down elevator until stall recovery is complete and stick shaker stops.
At bank angles greater than 67°, level flight cannot be maintained within AFM load factor limits.
It is important to not increase g force or use nose-up elevator or stabilizer until approaching wings level.

title: Windshear Escape Maneuver

flash.title: Short final, 600 ft, thunderstorm nearby, A/P engaged.
flash.text: Speed gains 20 kt then drops 25 kt, V/S goes to −1500 ft/min below the glide.
cues: IAS −15 kt / V/S −500 fpm / 1 dot G/S

steps.text: Call “WINDSHEAR GO” (Air Algérie SOP)
Disengage autopilot.
Push either TO/GA switch.
Aggressively apply maximum thrust
Disengage autothrottle.
Simultaneously roll wings level and rotate toward an initial pitch attitude of 15°.
Retract speedbrakes.
Follow flight director TO/GA guidance (if available) — Do not exceed the Pitch Limit Indication.
Push either TO/GA switch. Verify TO/GA mode annunciation. Verify GA thrust. Retract speedbrakes. Monitor system performance
MANUAL OR AUTOMATIC FLIGHT: Do not change flap or gear configuration until windshear is no longer a factor.
MANUAL OR AUTOMATIC FLIGHT: Maintain wings level to maximize climb gradient, unless a turn is required for obstacle clearance. Monitor vertical speed and altitude.
MANUAL OR AUTOMATIC FLIGHT: Do not attempt to regain lost airspeed until windshear is no longer a factor.
Verify maximum thrust (manual) / Verify GA thrust (automatic). Verify all needed actions have been completed and call out any omissions.
Monitor vertical speed and altitude. Call out any trend toward terrain contact, descending flight path, or significant airspeed changes.

nums.s: Then up to intermittent shaker / PLI
Unacceptable deviation < 1000 ft AGL (with 500 fpm, 5° pitch, 1 dot G/S)
Latest rotation if unable to stop

trap: Lowering the nose to “regain speed”: that's the crash. Hold the pitch (15°, up to intermittent shaker) and leave gear and flaps alone while windshear is a factor.
then: PWS caution (“MONITOR RADAR DISPLAY”): maneuver to avoid the windshear
PWS warning on approach (“GO-AROUND, WINDSHEAR AHEAD”): escape, or normal go-around at pilot's discretion
Windshear on takeoff roll before V1: at VR normal rotation toward 15°, escape once airborne
End: call windshear no longer a factor, transition to normal flight, retract gear/flaps per schedule (SOP)
TO/GA unavailable: disengage A/P and A/T and fly manually
diff: Same maneuver NG/MAX (QRH NG MAN.1.13 / MAX MAN.1.14). Nothing to adapt for the pilot.

qcm.q: Windshear warning on final, manual flight. Target initial pitch?
qcm.w: “rotate toward an initial pitch attitude of 15°” — 20° is the GPWS PULL UP.

qcm.q: “WINDSHEAR AHEAD, WINDSHEAR AHEAD” on takeoff roll, before V1:
o: Continue and fly the escape after rotation
qcm.w: Predictive windshear warning during takeoff roll: “before V1, reject takeoff · after V1, perform the Windshear Escape Maneuver”.

qcm.q: During the escape, speed keeps decreasing. The PF:
o: Lowers the nose to regain it
Does not try to regain speed while windshear is a factor
qcm.w: “Do not attempt to regain lost airspeed until windshear is no longer a factor.” Intermittent shaker is the upper pitch limit.

qcm.q: “Unacceptable” deviation below 1000 ft AGL: which is NOT on the QRH list?
qcm.w: QRH list: 15 kt IAS, 500 fpm V/S, 5° pitch, 1 dot G/S, unusual thrust lever position for a significant time. No bank.

qcm.q: In automatic flight, after pushing TO/GA, the PF:
o: Verify TO/GA mode annunciation, verify GA thrust
qcm.w: AUTOMATIC FLIGHT: TO/GA, “Verify TO/GA mode annunciation. Verify GA thrust. Retract speedbrakes. Monitor system performance”, ready to take over manually.

sources.quote: Aggressively apply maximum thrust* • Disengage autothrottle. • Simultaneously roll wings level and rotate toward an initial pitch attitude of 15 °.
Do not attempt to regain lost airspeed until windshear is no longer a factor.
Predictive windshear warning during takeoff roll: (“WINDSHEAR AHEAD, WINDSHEAR AHEAD” aural) • before V1, reject takeoff • after V1, perform the Windshear Escape Maneuver.
below 1000 feet AGL, in excess of any of the following: • 15 knots indicated airspeed • 500 fpm vertical speed • 5° pitch attitude • 1 dot displacement from the glideslope
initiate a normal rotation at least 2,000 feet before the end of the runway, even if airspeed is low.
When the Windshear Escape Maneuver is required, the PF shall call: "WINDSHEAR GO"

title: Rejected Takeoff

flash.title: Takeoff DAAG, wet runway, CPT PF, autobrake RTO.
flash.text: The F/O just called “EIGHTY KNOTS”. At 120 kt, V1 142, Master Caution comes on with a system light, then a dull thud.

steps.text: Announce “REJECT” (captain only decides) — decision in time to start the maneuver by V1
Without delay: Simultaneously close the thrust levers, disengage the autothrottles and apply maximum manual wheel brakes or verify operation of RTO autobrake.
If RTO autobrake is selected, monitor system performance and apply manual wheel brakes if the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light illuminates or deceleration is not adequate.
Raise SPEED BRAKE lever.
Apply reverse thrust up to the maximum amount consistent with conditions.
Continue maximum braking until certain the airplane can stop on the runway.
Verify actions as follows: Thrust levers closed. Autothrottles disengaged. Maximum brakes applied.
Verify SPEED BRAKE lever UP and call “SPEEDBRAKES UP.” If SPEED BRAKE lever is not UP, call “SPEEDBRAKES NOT UP.”

Reverse thrust applied. When both REV indications are green, call "REVERSERS NORMAL." If there is no REV indication(s) or the indication(s) stays amber, call "NO REVERSER ENGINE NUMBER 1", or "NO REVERSER ENGINE NUMBER 2", or "NO REVERSERS". Call out omitted action items.
Call out 60 knots.

When stopping is assured: Start movement of the reverse thrust levers to reach the reverse idle detent before taxi speed. After the engines are at reverse idle, move the reverse thrust levers to full down.
Communicate the reject decision to the control tower and cabin as soon as practical.

nums.s: Master caution, system failure, noise/vibration, tire, slow accel., config warning, fire, engine failure, PWS, window, unsafe airplane
Fire / fire warning, engine failure, PWS warning, airplane unsafe or unable to fly

trap: Rejecting above 80 kt for a Master Caution, or starting the stopping action after V1: #1 cause of runway excursions. And don't forget to disengage the A/T, or the thrust levers advance again if you reject before THR HLD.
then: F/O to ATC (below 60 kt or stopped): “AIR ALGERIE (call sign) REJECTED TAKEOFF AIRCRAFT ON THE RUNWAY” (SOP)
CPT on PA: “CABIN CREW NORMAL PROCEDURES” or “CABIN CREW AT YOUR STATIONS”
Memory items / NNC as per the cause; if needed “EVACUATION CHECKLIST” then “EVACUATE, EVACUATE, EVACUATE”
Brake Cooling Schedule, fuse plugs, parking brake only if evacuating, fire services, wind if fire
New takeoff: new “CABIN READY” required
diff: Same maneuver NG/MAX. Different QRH pages (NG MAN.1.2, MAX MAN.1.5). Wording nuance: “unless passenger evacuation is needed” (NG) / “is necessary” (MAX).

qcm.q: At 110 kt (V1 140), MASTER CAUTION only, no other symptom. Decision?
qcm.w: Above 80 kt and before V1, reject only for fire/fire warning, engine failure, PWS warning, or airplane unsafe/unable to fly.

qcm.q: Which is NOT a reason to reject between 80 kt and V1?
qcm.w: Tire failure is on the “before 80 knots” list only. Between 80 kt and V1: fire, engine failure, PWS warning, unsafe/unable to fly.

qcm.q: F/O PF, CPT calls “REJECT”. Who flies?
o: The F/O keeps control until a positive input by the CPT
The CPT from the callout, no other action
qcm.w: “the first officer maintains control of the airplane until the captain makes a positive input to the controls.”

qcm.q: Reversers: only one REV indication turns green. F/O callout?
qcm.w: If one REV indication is missing or stays amber: “NO REVERSER ENGINE NUMBER 1” or “NUMBER 2”; both: “NO REVERSERS”.

qcm.q: Why disengage the A/T on every RTO (FCTM)?
o: Before THR HLD, thrust levers would advance to takeoff thrust once released
qcm.w: Before THR HLD annunciates, without disengagement the thrust levers advance back to takeoff thrust. For consistency: A/T disengaged for all RTOs.

sources.quote: Above 80 knots and before V1, reject the takeoff for any of the following: • fire or fire warning • engine failure • predictive windshear warning • if the airplane is unsafe or unable to fly.
Simultaneously close the thrust levers, disengage the autothrottles and apply maximum manual wheel brakes or verify operation of RTO autobrake.
If the first officer is making the takeoff, the first officer maintains control of the airplane until the captain makes a positive input to the controls.
After THR HLD is annunciated, the thrust levers, when retarded, remain in idle. For procedural consistency, disconnect the autothrottle for all rejected takeoffs.

V1 means the maximum speed in the takeoff at which the pilot must take the first action (e.g., apply brakes, reduce thrust, deploy speedbrakes) to stop the airplane within the accelerate-stop distance
“AIR ALGERIE (Call sign) REJECTED TAKEOFF AIRCRAFT ON THE RUNWAY".

title: Overrun Warnings (ORW)
ref: QRH MAX MAN.1.4–1.5 · FCOM MAX L.10 / 15.20.13–14

flash.title: MAX, approach to a short wet runway, tailwind.
flash.text: A bit high and fast at 300 ft, you push to regain the path. Then, on the ground, the autobrake feels weak.

steps.phase: In-Air Overrun Warning (OVERRUN, GO-AROUND / GO-AROUND on PFD)
steps.text: Execute a go-around.
Simultaneously close the thrust levers and apply maximum manual wheel brakes.
Verify speed brakes are deployed or raise the SPEED BRAKE lever.
Apply reverse thrust up to the maximum amount consistent with conditions.
Continue maximum braking until certain the airplane can stop on the runway.
Verify actions as follows: Thrust levers closed. Maximum brakes applied.
Verify SPEED BRAKE lever UP and call “SPEEDBRAKES UP.” If SPEED BRAKE lever is not UP, call “SPEEDBRAKES NOT UP.”

Reverse thrust applied. When both REV indications are green, call "REVERSERS NORMAL." If there is no REV indication(s) or the indication(s) stays amber, call "NO REVERSER ENGINE NUMBER 1", or "NO REVERSER ENGINE NUMBER 2", or "NO REVERSERS". Call out omitted action items.
Call out 60 knots.

When stopping is assured: Start movement of the reverse thrust levers to reach the reverse idle detent before taxi speed. After the engines are at reverse idle, move the reverse thrust levers to full down.

nums.s: GS < 20 kt or 1000 ft from runway end
If ≤ 150 ft TDZE and alert valid ≥ 7 s

trap: Believing no alert = guaranteed stop. The FCOM is clear: ORW does not replace the en-route landing distance assessment, and no alert does not guarantee stopping before the runway end.
then: “OVERRUN, GO-AROUND” on approach: immediate go-around
Inhibit ORW if ground OAT < −40 °C or > 50 °C, or weight > MLW (FCOM MAX)
The “MAX BRAKES, MAX REVERSE” aural sounds only once
Based on the EGPWS runway database and airplane position
diff: MAX only: ORW and its maneuver do not exist in the NG QRH (rev 55).

qcm.q: “OVERRUN, GO-AROUND” at 200 ft. Action?
qcm.w: In-Air Overrun Warning: “Execute a go-around.” (PF and PM).

qcm.q: “MAX BRAKES, MAX REVERSE” on the rollout. PF's first action?
o: Simultaneously close the thrust levers and apply maximum manual wheel brakes
Raise SPEED BRAKE lever, then brake
qcm.w: “Without delay: Simultaneously close the thrust levers and apply maximum manual wheel brakes.”

qcm.q: In-Air ORW is armed from:
qcm.w: FCOM MAX: “The alert is armed from 500 feet above the runway touchdown zone elevation (TDZE) until airplane touchdown.”

qcm.q: When must ORW be inhibited (FCOM)?
qcm.w: Inhibit if ground OAT < −40 °C or > 50 °C, or weight > Maximum Landing Weight.

qcm.q: No ORW alert on a short runway. Conclusion?
o: Nothing is guaranteed: landing distance assessment is still mandatory
qcm.w: “The lack of an overrun alert does not guarantee the airplane can stop prior to reaching the runway end.”

sources.quote: In-Air Overrun Warning … • OVERRUN, GO-AROUND aural alert • GO-AROUND annunciation on the PFD … Execute a go-around.
Without delay: Simultaneously close the thrust levers and apply maximum manual wheel brakes.
The lack of an overrun alert does not guarantee the airplane can stop prior to reaching the runway end.
Inhibit the overrun alert when: • Landing OAT on the ground is below –40°C or greater than 50°C; or • Gross Weight is greater than Maximum Landing Weight.
The alert is armed from three seconds after touchdown until the airplane slows below 20 knots ground speed, or comes within 1000 feet of the runway end.

title: Runway Awareness and Advisory System (RAAS)
ref: QRH MAN.1.8 (MAX) / MAN.1.4 (NG) · FCOM NG L.10.9

flash.title: Night taxi, unfamiliar airport, parallel runway.
flash.text: You line up on what you think is the cleared runway. The voice callout doesn't match your briefing.

steps.text: If a RAAS callout or alert differs from the flight crew’s expectation: Verify position. Contact ATC for assistance, if needed.

trap: Using RAAS as a navigation aid or for performance decisions: prohibited. It replaces neither NOTAM nor ATIS, and the announced runway length ignores weather and runway condition.
then: Do not use RAAS for navigation
Not a substitute for NOTAM / ATIS
Runway length alert set by the operator, no real-time factors
diff: QRH NG: RAAS limited by effectivity to airplanes YD111–YD117 and YG721–YV388 (see FCOM NG 0.1 for registrations). QRH MAX: no effectivity restriction.

qcm.q: The RAAS callout doesn't match the expected runway. QRH action?
o: Ignore it, RAAS is advisory only
Verify position. Contact ATC for assistance, if needed.
qcm.w: QRH: “Verify position. Contact ATC for assistance, if needed.” (PF and PM).

qcm.q: Can a RAAS runway length alert be used to assess performance?
o: Yes, if the runway is dry
No: set by the operator, no weather, runway condition or NOTAM
qcm.w: FCOM NG: “Do not use … RAAS … to determine real-time runway suitability for airplane performance.”

qcm.q: Can RAAS replace ATIS or NOTAM?
qcm.w: “Do not use RAAS callouts or alerts as a substitute for NOTAM or ATIS information.”

qcm.q: Prohibited use of RAAS per FCOM NG:
qcm.w: “Do not use RAAS callouts or alerts for navigation.”

qcm.q: On the Air Algérie NG fleet, RAAS is:
o: Installed on the whole NG fleet
Not installed on the NG fleet
qcm.w: The NG QRH and FCOM list RAAS effectivity as YD111 - YD117, YG721 - YV388.

sources.quote: Accomplish the following if a RAAS callout or alert differs from the flight crew’s expectation: … Verify position. Contact ATC for assistance, if needed.
Runway Awareness and Advisory System (RAAS) YD111 - YD117, YG721 - YV388
Do not use RAAS callouts or alerts for navigation. Do not use RAAS callouts or alerts as a substitute for NOTAM or ATIS information.
RAAS runway length alerting is set by airline policy and does not consider real-time factors such as weather, runway conditions, or Notices to Airmen (NOTAMS).
